Several Midwest Vitro facilities were at end of life and slated for decommissioning, but an agreement with First Solar enabled modernization and expansion of these facilities (Crowell 2023). Japan- headquartered Nippon Sheet Glass Group is known to supply gigawatt-level volumes of TCO- coated front glass from a float glass line in Ohio (Jacobo 2025c). Around 21 float glass facilities are in the United States, of which approximately seven contain two lines. This corresponds to 30 float glass lines in total (National Glass Association 2025). The companies operating float lines are Vitro, Cardinal, Guardian, Pilkington NSG, NSG Group, and AGC (Asahi Glass Company) (National Glass Association 2025). As indicated by the expansion and investments into the lines in Ohio and Pennsylvania, it is possible to convert existing float glass lines to TCO glass production if market drivers materialize. 3.5.3 Imports/Exports of CdTe PV Glass As described above, domestic capacity of TCO float glass is sufficient to meet CdTe manufacturing demand. The rear glass, which is not TCO-coated and can be rolled or float, may be imported. See Section 2.8.3 for more information on glass imports and exports. 3.5.4 Pricing for CdTe PV Glass First Solar has entered into multiyear agreements with NSG and Vitro to provide front glass, but the price has not been disclosed. Bottom-up modeling estimated that CdTe front and back glass cost approximately $0.053/W or $9.42/m2 for a Series 6 module from Southeast Asia in 2020 dc (Smith, Woodhouse, Horowitz, et al. 2021b). This approximately aligns with front TCO glass costs provided by Roth Capital (Philip Shen 2025) of $7–$9/m2, who also estimated $3–$5/m2 for rear glass. Because of the TCO coating, front glass is always more expensive than rear, uncoated glass. For solar applications, float glass is generally understood to be more expensive than rolled glass. Discussions with U.S. float glass producers in 2021 indicated this is partly because the float line must be slowed significantly to reduce impurity incorporation for high transmittance of sunlight (Basore and Feldman 2022b). However, monofacial CdTe modules can tolerate more impurities in rear glass, which may enable domestic float glass lines to supply rear glass at higher line speeds and more competitive costs. 3.5.5 Upstream Inputs for CdTe PV Glass This section provides some limited information on priority inputs for CdTe PV glass production. Many other upstream inputs are not discussed here due to limited supply chain information or relatively low importance such as dolomite, lime, pot ash, alumina, and material needed for antireflective coatings. • Cullet: See Section 2.8.5.
